title: First Who... Then What
coreMove: Resolve people fit before locking strategy so the organization can adapt without coercion.
sourcePressure: The source reverses the normal strategy sequence: first who, then what. Right people create adaptability under uncertainty, and the right seat matters alongside raw talent.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version turns this into ordinary hiring advice, talent worship, or permission to treat people harshly.

counterintuition: people matter more than strategy as a slogan

exampleSpecs.domain: polar research station winter crew selection
exampleSpecs.audience: an expedition lead choosing a six-person winter crew before the final research agenda is approved
exampleSpecs.stakes: once the ice closes, the wrong temperament cannot be managed away
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the lead removes the strongest glacier specialist from the roster after watching him dismiss the radio tech's weather concern, then keeps the adaptable mechanic before choosing the field route
exampleSpecs.firstImage: freeze-dried meal crates lined beneath a station window crusted with ice

exampleSpecs.audience: a co-op board deciding whether to launch a winter subscription box
exampleSpecs.stakes: the crop plan will change twice, so the shed leads must handle ambiguity without resentment
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the board reviews a spoiled-spinach incident and sees that the quiet pallet lead redesigned the cold-room flow while the star salesperson blamed growers
exampleSpecs.firstImage: spinach bins beading water on a cold-room scale

exampleSpecs.audience: an editor building a team before picking the first target of a yearlong investigation
exampleSpecs.stakes: a brittle reporter can wreck source trust before the story direction is clear
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the editor pauses topic selection and moves the court-records reporter into lead after hearing how she corrected a source without humiliating him
exampleSpecs.firstImage: sealed court-file envelopes stacked under a desk lamp

exampleSpecs.audience: an EMS director planning a new coverage model
exampleSpecs.stakes: a map cannot compensate for medics who undermine each other at 3 a.m.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the director delays the coverage-map vote and first swaps a brilliant paramedic out of night command after watching dispatch audio where he leaves a trainee isolated
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a dispatch waveform frozen on a monitor beside a half-finished coverage map

exampleSpecs.audience: a chief conservator choosing staff before committing to a fragile textile exhibition
exampleSpecs.stakes: the exhibition schedule depends on people who can admit uncertainty before damage is permanent
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she gives the lead seat to the assistant who stopped a dye test and asked for help, then postpones the exhibition theme until the lab team is right
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a silk fragment resting under a magnifying lamp

exampleSpecs.audience: a clinic director deciding whether to add immigration cases
exampleSpecs.stakes: clients will be harmed if the clinic expands before the right case managers are in place
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the director shelves the expansion flyer and first moves the bilingual intake coordinator into triage because she spots deadline risk before attorneys do
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a stack of unopened court notices held with a green rubber band

skillTargets: choose people sequence before strategy sequence
identify seat mismatch versus talent shortage
judge when adaptability matters more than a fixed plan

tryThisNowSpec: Name one plan you are about to finalize. Before editing the plan, write the two seats that must be right for the plan to survive a surprise.

sourceAnchors.name: first who, then what
sourceAnchors.detail: the source presents the reversal as getting the right people on the bus before fixing the final route
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: First who, then what is not a hiring slogan; it is how a team stays useful when the map changes.
